report.source_text: Physical examination showed that best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of counting finger at one and three meters in the right and left eyes respectively. Average repeated IOP measured by I- care tonometer was 12 mmHg for right eye and 11 mmHg in the left eye. Pupils were equal in size and reactive to light, there was no relative afferent pupillary defect. Horizontal corneal diameter was 14mm (Figure 1) in both eyes with stromal opacities and Haab's striae (Figure 2). Anterior chambers were deep and gonioscopy revealed wide open angles in both eyes. There was iridodonesis, phacodonesis, as well as superiorly and nasally subluxated cataract lenses in both eyes. The cataract in the right eye was denser.

report.source_text: After counseling and discussion on prognosis with the patient, manual small incision cataract surgery was done for the right eye. On 2nd post-operative week, the right eye BCVA was 6/36 and poor vision was explained by amblyopia. After one month the IOP was normal, but intraocular lens (IOL) was dislocated and BCVA decreased to 6/60.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 32-year-old Ethiopian man presented in June 2019 with 2-year progressive vision loss, having had low vision and large eyes (buphthalmos) since childhood without family history of consanguinity. Examination revealed severe visual impairment (CF at 1m OD, CF at 3m OS), bilateral buphthalmos (14mm horizontal corneal diameter), Haab's striae with stromal opacities, deep anterior chambers, and wide open angles. Intraocular pressure was normal (12 mmHg OD, 11 mmHg OS), indicating spontaneous arrest of congenital glaucoma. Bilateral lens subluxation was evident with iridodonesis, phacodonesis, and superior/nasal subluxation, denser in the right eye. Optic disc examination showed healthy rims (VCDR 0.6) without nerve fiber layer loss and normal visual fields. Right eye underwent manual small incision cataract surgery, achieving BCVA 6/36 at week 2 (limited by amblyopia), but developed IOL dislocation by month 1 with BCVA declining to 6/60 while IOP remained normal.

Buphthalmos evidenced by 14mm horizontal corneal diameter bilaterally with Haab's striae and stromal opacities consistent with congenital glaucoma
Spontaneously arrested glaucoma status evidenced by normal IOP (11-12 mmHg) despite buphthalmos signs
Absence of progressive glaucomatous optic neuropathy evidenced by pink rims, VCDR 0.6, no NFL loss, and normal visual fields
